All right, I've just finished the interactive TUI smoke test. I added the "/help" link to the status bar, inserted the new “Goals that get checked” card, and verified that the UI responds correctly to input. The live tps numbers looked reasonable (≈400–600 tok/s), which suggests the Groq backend is performing as expected. 

Now I need to tidy up the temporary tmux session I created for the test. Leaving it running would waste resources and could interfere with any subsequent tests or builds. The cleanest way is to kill the session outright with `tmux kill-session -t glinttest`. 

Next, I should make sure that the recent edits to `site/index.html` haven't broken the build. Running `bun run build` will compile the project, but I don't need the verbose build logs in the chat—just confirmation that it succeeded. So I’ll redirect both stdout and stderr to `/dev/null`. 

Finally, to confirm the build produced a working binary, I’ll execute the newly built `glint` executable with `--version`. This will give a quick, deterministic output that I can report back (or at least know that the binary runs). 

I’ll combine these steps into a single Bash command: kill the tmux session, run the build silently, and then, if the build succeeded, run the version check. I’ll also set a generous timeout (3 minutes) to accommodate the build time on this machine. 

Thus the appropriate tool call is a Bash execution with the command:
`tmux kill-session -t glinttest; bun run build >/dev/null 2>&1 && ./dist/glint --version`, 
a description indicating cleanup, build, and version check, and a timeout of 180000 ms.
